segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After this Jesus went about in Galilee. He did not want to go about in Judea, because the Judeans were seeking to kill him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the Jews’ Festival of Booths was near.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So his brothers said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Leave here and go to Judea, so that your disciples too may see the works you are doing.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For no one does anything in secret while he himself seeks to be in the open. If you are doing these things, show yourself to the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For not even his brothers believed in him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My time has not yet arrived, but your time is always ready.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it that its works are evil.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You go up to the festival. I am not going up to this festival, because my time has not yet been fulfilled.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Having said this, he stayed behind in Galilee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when his brothers had gone up to the festival, then he too went up, not publicly but, as it were, in secret.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jewish leaders were looking for him at the festival and saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where is that man?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was much murmuring about him among the crowds. Some were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He is a good man.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Others were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “No, he is leading the crowd astray.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Yet no one spoke openly about him, for fear of the Jewish leaders.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the festival was already half over, Jesus went up to the temple and began to teach.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jewish leaders were amazed and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How is this man so learned, when he has never studied?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My teaching is not mine but belongs to the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone is willing to do his will, that person will know about the teaching, whether it is from God or whether I speak on my own.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The one who speaks on his own seeks his own glory; but the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there is no falsehood in him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Did not Moses give you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why are you seeking to kill me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The crowd answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You have a demon! Who is seeking to kill you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I did one work, and you are all amazed.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For this reason Moses has given you circumcision—not that it comes from Moses, but from the fathers—and you circumcise a person on the Sabbath.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If a person receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses is not broken, are you angry with me because I made a whole person well on the Sabbath?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do not judge by appearance, but judge with just judgment.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So some of the people of Jerusalem were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Is this not the man they are seeking to kill?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And look, he is speaking openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers have truly come to know that this is the Messiah?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But we know where this man is from; when the Messiah comes, no one knows where he is from.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus cried out as he was teaching in the temple,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know me, and you know where I am from. Yet I have not come on my own; rather, the one who sent me is true, and you do not know him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they were seeking to seize him, yet no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But many of the crowd believed in him, and they were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “When the Messiah comes, surely he will not do more signs than this man has done?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things about him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am with you a little while longer, and then I am going to the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You will look for me and will not find me, and where I am you cannot come.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where does this man intend to go, that we will not find him? Surely he does not intend to go to the Diaspora among the Greeks and teach the Greeks?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: What is this saying of his, ‘You will look for me and will not find me, and where I am you cannot come’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the last day, the great day of the festival, Jesus stood and cried out,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever believes in me, as the scripture has said, ‘Rivers of living water will flow from within him.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now he said this about the Spirit, which those who had believed in him were going to receive; for as yet there was no Spirit, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So some of the crowd, when they heard these words, were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This truly is the Prophet.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Others were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This is the Messiah.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But some were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely the Messiah does not come from Galilee?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Has not the scripture said that the Messiah comes from the offspring of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So a division arose in the crowd because of him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, who said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why did you not bring him?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The officers answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Never has a person spoken like this!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Pharisees answered them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely you have not been led astray as well?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Has any of the rulers believed in him, or any of the Pharisees?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But this crowd that does not know the law—they are accursed.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nicodemus, the one who had come to him earlier and who was one of them, said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely our law does not judge a person without first hearing from him and finding out what he is doing?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely you are not from Galilee too? Search and see that no prophet arises from Galilee.”

notes.note: The Greek word names a people with a religion and a homeland, and John uses it in more than one way. Here the contrast is geographic, Judea as against Galilee, so 'Judeans' is used. In verses 11, 13 and 15 the group is the Jerusalem authorities, as opposed to the festival crowds, who were themselves Jewish, so 'the Jewish leaders' is used there. Most translations have 'the Jews' throughout, and scholars are divided on the best English.

This was the week-long autumn pilgrimage festival (Sukkot), when people lived in temporary shelters to recall the wilderness years and to celebrate the harvest. 'Booths' is used because 'tabernacles' no longer suggests a hut to most readers. Later Jewish sources describe daily water-pouring rites at this festival, which may lie behind Jesus's words about thirst and living water in verses 37–38.

notes.traditional: I am not yet going up
notes.note: Many manuscripts, including some of the earliest, read 'not yet' instead of 'not'. Many editors prefer 'not' as the harder reading, which scribes may have softened because Jesus does go up in verse 10; others regard 'not yet' as original. The decision is disputed.

The Greek says literally that he 'knows letters', an idiom for being educated. The surprise is not that Jesus can read but that he teaches Scripture like a trained scholar without having studied under a recognised teacher.

These words can be attached to the end of verse 21 instead: 'you are all amazed because of it. Moses has given you circumcision…'. Several modern translations take them that way or leave them untranslated. The rendering here follows the punctuation of the Greek edition being translated, on which Jesus points to circumcision on the Sabbath as given with a purpose that his healing fulfils.
Greek has one word-family where English has two (righteous/just, righteousness/justice). Since the subject here is judging fairly, 'just' is used. Older translations have 'righteous judgment'.

The Greek word means the anointed king Israel expected, and in this chapter it is a title under debate, not a name. 'Messiah' conveys that to a modern reader; 'Christ' is kept where the word functions as a name for Jesus. Several modern translations make the same distinction.

The 'Diaspora' was the standard term for Jews living scattered outside the land of Israel, here those in the Greek-speaking world. The speakers wonder, scornfully, whether Jesus will go abroad to those communities and even teach non-Jews. 'Greeks' here means Greek-speaking Gentiles.

The Greek can be punctuated differently: 'Let anyone who is thirsty come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink. As the scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within him', in which case the rivers flow from Jesus, not from the believer. Both readings are ancient and both have scholarly support. The translation follows the punctuation of the Greek edition used, which is also the more common reading.

The Greek word means the belly or womb and was also used for a person's inner self; many modern versions have 'heart' or 'from within'. No single Old Testament passage matches the quotation. It probably draws together several texts about water flowing in the wilderness and from the temple, and which ones are meant is disputed.

notes.phrase: as yet there was no Spirit
notes.traditional: the Spirit was not yet given
notes.note: The Greek says simply 'there was not yet Spirit'. Most translations add 'given', as some later manuscripts do. John has already spoken of the Spirit descending on Jesus, so the meaning is not that the Spirit did not exist but that the Spirit was not yet present with believers in the way that followed Jesus's glorification.
This is not 'a prophet' but a particular expected figure: the prophet like Moses promised in Deuteronomy 18:15–18. In John the crowds treat this figure as distinct from the Messiah (compare 1:20–21).

candidates.reason: It ranges across 'openly', 'plainly', 'boldly' and 'confidence' in John, Acts, Paul and Hebrews, and translators vary widely, so the senses need fixing once.
It is rendered variously as officers, guards, temple police, attendants, servants and ministers across the Gospels, Acts and 1 Corinthians, and the reader should see one word per sense.
'Deceive', 'lead astray', 'mislead' and 'go astray' compete across the Gospels, the letters and Revelation, and the charge of leading the people astray is a recurring technical accusation.
'Rulers', 'authorities', 'leaders' and 'officials' are all in use for Jewish council members, civic magistrates and spiritual powers, and consistency by sense is needed.
It occurs here and in James 1:1 and 1 Peter 1:1, where 'Dispersion', 'Diaspora' and 'scattered' compete, and it should be decided whether the established English word 'Diaspora' is used throughout.
